In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the probability of recovering ED after surgery is lower in patients with preoperative functional impairment, depression and those receiving aRT.
aRT should be considered in patients who have a high risk of disease recurrence and in whom the risk of disease recurrence outweighs the risk of ED.
aRT should not be considered as a standard of care for patients with high risk PCa, but only for patients with a high risk of relapse.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients who are not depressed and have a good preoperative EF have better outcomes after BNSRP.
a preoperative IHEF-EF score of ⩾21, absence of depressive symptoms and lack of postoperative aRT should be considered as positive predictors for EF recovery after BNSRP.
aRT should not be administered to men with good baseline EF and without depression.
The main takeaway from our work is that

depression and functional status should be taken into consideration when counseling PCa survivors regarding the long-term consequences of BNSRP, whereas the administration of a RT has a negative impact on the likelihood of recovering EF.
patients with a preoperative functional status and/or depression should be considered for alternative therapies such as brachytherapy or external-beam radiotherapy.
